```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(ggplot2)
library(leaflet)
library(scales)
library(caret)       # pour la division train/test et les métriques
library(rpart)       # pour le modèle arbre
library(rpart.plot) 
library(broom)

#step 1

df=read.csv("train.csv")
glimpse(df)

df$last_review=ymd(df$last_review)

df$reviews_per_month[is.na(df$reviews_per_month)]=0
df$price=as.numeric(df$price)
df=df %>% filter(price > 0)

cols_to_remove=c("id", "host_id", "host_name")
df=df %>% select(-any_of(cols_to_remove))
sapply(df, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))
sum(df$availability_365==0)
glimpse(df)
write.csv(df, "train_cleaned.csv", row.names = FALSE)


#step 2

df <- read.csv("train_cleaned.csv")
df$log_price <- log1p(df$price)
most_recent_date <- max(ymd(df$last_review), na.rm = TRUE)
df$days_since_last_review <- as.numeric(
  difftime(most_recent_date, ymd(df$last_review), units = "days")
)
table(df$neighbourhood)
table(df$neighbourhood_group)
df$room_type <- as.factor(df$room_type)
glimpse(df)
write.csv(df, "train_transformed.csv", row.names = FALSE)


#step 3


df <- read.csv("train_transformed.csv")
glimpse(df)
leaflet(df) %>%
  addTiles() %>%
  addCircleMarkers(
    ~longitude, ~latitude,
    color = ~case_when(
      neighbourhood_group == "Manhattan" ~ "red",
      neighbourhood_group == "Brooklyn" ~ "blue",
      neighbourhood_group == "Queens" ~ "green",
      neighbourhood_group == "Bronx" ~ "purple",
      neighbourhood_group == "Staten Island" ~ "orange",
      TRUE ~ "gray"
    ),
    radius = 5,
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.5,
    popup = ~paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>",
                    "Price: $", price, "<br>",
                    "Room type: ", room_type, "<br>",
                    "Neighbourhood: ", neighbourhood)
  )


ggplot(df, aes(x = reorder(neighbourhood_group, log_price, median), 
               y = log_price, fill = neighbourhood_group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +   
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set3") +
  labs(title = "Price distribution (log) by Borough",
       x = "Borough", y = "log(Price)") +
  theme_minimal() 



ggplot(df, aes(x = room_type, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "Number of Listings by Room Type",
       x = "Room Type", y = "Number of Listings") +
  theme_minimal()


ggplot(df, aes(x = availability_365, y = number_of_reviews)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.05, color = "darkblue") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red", se = FALSE) +
  labs(title = "Availability vs Reviews",
       x = "Availability (days per year)",
       y = "Number of Reviews") +
  theme_light()


df %>%
  group_by(neighbourhood_group, room_type) %>%
  summarise(mean_price = mean(price, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = neighbourhood_group, y = mean_price, fill = room_type)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "dodge") +
  labs(title = "Average Price by Room Type and Borough",
       x = "Borough", y = "Average Price ($)") +
  theme_minimal()

ggplot(df, aes(x = neighbourhood_group, fill = neighbourhood_group)) +
  geom_bar() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
  labs(title = "Number of Listings by Borough",
       x = "Borough", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()


#step 4


df <- read.csv("train_transformed.csv")

############################################################
# 1️⃣ Préparation des données pour le modèle
############################################################

# Retirer les lignes manquantes sur les variables utilisées
df_model <- df %>%
  select(log_price, neighbourhood_group, room_type, number_of_reviews) %>%
  drop_na()

# Division du dataset : 80% train / 20% test
set.seed(123)
train_index <- createDataPartition(df_model$log_price, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train <- df_model[train_index, ]
test  <- df_model[-train_index, ]

############################################################
# 2️⃣ Modèle 1 : Régression Linéaire
############################################################

model_lm <- lm(log_price ~ neighbourhood_group + room_type + number_of_reviews, data = train)

# Résumé du modèle
summary(model_lm)

# Prédictions
pred_lm_log <- predict(model_lm, newdata = test)

# Revenir à l’échelle du prix original (expm1 = inverse de log1p)
pred_lm_price <- expm1(pred_lm_log)

# Calcul du RMSE
rmse_lm <- sqrt(mean((test$log_price - pred_lm_log)^2))
cat("RMSE (Linear Model):", round(rmse_lm, 3), "\n")

############################################################
# 3️⃣ Modèle 2 : Arbre de Régression (rpart)
############################################################

model_tree <- rpart(log_price ~ neighbourhood_group + room_type + number_of_reviews,
                    data = train,
                    method = "anova",
                    control = rpart.control(cp = 0.01))

# Visualisation de l’arbre
rpart.plot(model_tree, type = 3, fallen.leaves = TRUE,
           main = "Regression Tree for Airbnb Prices")

# Prédictions
pred_tree_log <- predict(model_tree, newdata = test)
pred_tree_price <- expm1(pred_tree_log)

# Calcul du RMSE
rmse_tree <- sqrt(mean((test$log_price - pred_tree_log)^2))
cat("RMSE (Decision Tree):", round(rmse_tree, 3), "\n")

############################################################
# 4️⃣ Comparaison et interprétation
############################################################

cat("\n--- MODEL COMPARISON ---\n")
cat("Linear Regression RMSE:", round(rmse_lm, 3), "\n")
cat("Decision Tree RMSE:", round(rmse_tree, 3), "\n")

# Analyse des coefficients du modèle linéaire
coef_df <- tidy(model_lm)
print(coef_df)



# Interprétation basique à ajouter dans le rapport :
# - neighbourhood_group : Manhattan et Brooklyn augmentent significativement le prix
# - room_type : les Entire home/apt sont les plus chers
# - number_of_reviews : faible effet négatif (plus de reviews = prix légèrement plus bas)

```
